engine: gapsystudio's services 'product on a pedestal' — a staged object floating above a red plinth that (1) IDLES with a slow float + tiny rotate (always-on) and (2) TILTS toward the pointer (rotateX/rotateY parallax in a CSS perspective scene), the pedestal + a chrome ring reacting at a shallower depth. Harvested from D_gapsy (D /services: glass card + red shapes + icons on a red pedestal, slow orbit/parallax).
honesty: NO-WebGL APPROXIMATION. The original is live 3D (WebGL) — we do NOT copy that. This recreates the FEEL with CSS 3D transforms on a flat object image + a CSS-built pedestal: pointer-tilt + idle float + depth parallax. It is an approximation of an orbiting 3D product, NOT a real 3D mesh (precedent: the quadro pre-rendered 3D-viewer). For a fuller round-trip, swap the object for a pre-rendered turntable frame driven by the pointer (see room-dolly-scroll frame-scrub).

measured_teardown.move: a CSS perspective scene (transform-style: preserve-3d). The object eases (lerp) toward a tilt target: rotateY = pointerX(-1..1) * maxTilt, rotateX = -pointerY * maxTilt; plus an idle float translateY = sin(t)*float and a tiny idle rotate. The pedestal tilts at maxTilt*depth and the ring at maxTilt*(depth+0.2) — a shallower parallax so the object reads as in front. rAF gated by an IntersectionObserver (pauses off-screen). reduced-motion -> static.
measured_teardown.cited: gapsy /services: a red stacked pedestal with a glass card + red shapes + small icons (magnifier for UX Audit, brain+gears 'AI' for Visual Identity) on top, slowly orbiting / parallaxing as you move.

maxTilt.what: how far the object rotates to the pointer at the scene edge.

depth.what: pedestal tilt = object tilt * depth (the ring = depth+0.2). Lower = more separation/parallax between object and base.

float.what: amplitude of the idle vertical float (sin loop).

lerp.what: easing toward the tilt target (lower = laggier, heavier feel).

idle.what: run the always-on float + tiny rotate (off => only pointer-tilt).

entry: FloatingProductOrbit.create(target, opts) -> { set(px,py), start(), stop(), destroy }. target = .fpo-stage (perspective) > .fpo-scene (preserve-3d) > .fpo-object(img) + .fpo-pedestal + optional .fpo-ring. pointermove tilts; set(px,py 0..1) manually drives the tilt (PURE, for previews/snapshots).
law: transform: perspective rotateX/rotateY/translateY only; GPU; NO mix-blend over the object; NO WebGL; rAF gated by an IntersectionObserver (pauses off-screen); reduced-motion -> static. owns_pin false, owns_scroll false (a hover/idle primitive). The pedestal + ring are CSS-built (gradients + border), the object is a flat image — no 3D mesh.
gate_mode: triggered hover + always-on idle (not scroll). Verify: the object float changes over time (idle); set(1,0.5) rotates the object ~+maxTilt and the pedestal ~maxTilt*depth (shallower); set(0,0.5) flips the sign. Smoothness via pointer-move over the scene (the rAF idle+tilt is the cost). GATE-BLINDSPOT: a static screenshot can't show the idle/tilt — verify the transform values + fps.
proven: lab: OUR QUADRO macro render as the object on a CSS red pedestal + chrome ring. Measured live: idle float translateY 7.09px -> 9.73px over 0.5s (always-on); set(1,0.5) -> object rotateY +17.16deg, pedestal rotateY +6.72deg (=16*0.42 depth, shallower); set(0,0.5) -> object rotateY -14.81deg (sign flips).
